'''Tionese''', also called '''Old Tionese''', was formerly the language of the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]]. It was eventually replaced by [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]]. 
==History==
The word [[Vigo/Legends|vigo]] meant "nephew" in Old Tionese, and was adopted as a rank in the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] criminal organization.<ref name="ShadowsSB">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref>

While the worlds of the Tion Cluster were joining the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the langauge was replaced by the [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], and with time was reduced to a ceremonial and ritualistic one. It remained an official language only in the [[Kingdom of Barseg]], even during the [[Draggulch Period]]. It continued to be used in special occasions within the [[Cygnus Star Empire]], itself formed by defectors from [[Xim's empire]].<ref name="Written Word" />
==Writing==
The Tionese language used for writing the complex logographic system of the [[Cronese]]. The alphabet later known as "Tionese" had its origins in the [[Livien League]]. Its capital, [[Desevro/Legends|Desevro]], orbited a [[Binary star system/Legends|binary]] [[Desev system|star system]] and used letters as designation for its suns, [[Desev Alpha]] and [[Desev Beta]]. When [[Xim/Legends|Xim]] conquered Desevro, [[Xim's empire|his empire]] absorbed Deservar bureaucracy and its much more efficient alphabetic system. Thus it was adapted into the Old Tionese alphabet, which, thanks to Xim's conquests, it spread beyond the Cluster; such as the practice of using astronomical deignations in that alphabet, as originated on Desevro.<ref name="Written Word" />

During the [[Tionese War]], [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]] was used as a military outpost by the empire; the Alsakanese adopted the Tionese alphabet and in turn adapted it as the [[High Galactic/Legends|High Galactic alphabet]].<ref name="Written Word" />

Even when the Tionese language was dying out, the alphabet persisted, and Tionese calligraphy remained an art form in the Cluster.<ref name="Written Word" />

By the last centuries of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], its usage was reduced to designating names with its letter names, such as for military units and meneuvers. Its letters were used by organizations such as the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], which used them to designate its [[Squadron/Legends|squadrons]].<ref name="Written Word" />

The practice of designating starships with Tionese letter-names originated with [[Lianna/Legends|Lianna]]-based [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] products by [[Sienar Technologies]] in the Kingdom of Barseg; this was imitated by its partner [[Cygnus Spaceworks/Legends|Cygnus Spaceworks]], in the Cygnus Star Empire. The practice was followed also by [[Telgorn Corporation/Legends|Telgorn]] and [[Kuat Systems Engineering/Legends|Kuat Systems Engineering]].<ref name="Written Word" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|It appears that multiple alphabets are in common use, as is evidenced by the existence of names and terms such as R2-D2, attack pattern Delta, ''Lambda''-class shuttle, ''Aleph''-class starfighters, and others stemming from the more visible Aurebesh written script.|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|<ref name="Insider">{{InsiderCite|90|Star Wars Q&A|Ask the Master}}</ref>}}
This article describes the instances of the [[Wikipedia:Greek Alphabet|Greek alphabet]] in the ''[[Star Wars]]'' canon. Greek letter names are frequently used both in real life and in science fiction to designate ships, technology, constellations, etc.

The [[2010]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] article ''[[The Written Word]]'' reveals that this is in fact the Tionese alphabet, which would eventually lose popularity in favor of Galactic Basic.<ref name="Written Word" />

The Greek letter names listed above are only those explicitly stated by ''The Written Word'' as being derived from Tionese. Other designations that appear in [[Star Wars]] that derive from the real-life Greek alphabet include [[Gamma (disambiguation)|Gamma]], [[Epsilon (disambiguation)|Epsilon]], [[Eta (disambiguation)|Eta]], [[Xi (disambiguation)|Xi]], and so on.
